status_summary: No CMS plan to separate the subsidized and non-subsidized markets was found. The 2027 Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters final rule (91 FR 29526), published 2026-05-20 and effective 2026-07-20, gives some relief from ACA plan rules for plan year 2027, including bronze plan cost-sharing flexibility in the individual market, removal of standardized plan options, multi-year catastrophic plans and a hardship route into catastrophic coverage for people ineligible for subsidies by income; its provisions are framed largely around Exchange enrollment and do not create separate rules for off-exchange coverage, so this is a parallel step, not a separation of the markets. The Marketplace Integrity and Affordability final rule of 2025-06-25 tightens enrollment verification in the subsidized exchanges and applies no separate rules to the two markets.

timeline.event: CMS published the 2027 Notice of Benefit and Payment Parameters final rule (91 FR 29526, effective 2026-07-20), which for plan year 2027 lets individual market bronze plans exceed the standard cost-sharing limit by up to 130 percent, removes standardized plan option requirements, permits catastrophic plan terms of up to ten years, and widens a hardship exemption so people ineligible for premium tax credits or cost-sharing reductions because income is below 100 percent or above 250 percent of the poverty level may enroll in catastrophic coverage; the catastrophic and hardship provisions are framed around Exchange enrollment.

title: Plan to separate the unsubsidized individual market from the subsidized ACA exchange
uncertainties: Mandate text on pages 469 and 470 was checked. The Marketplace Integrity final rule page was truncated, so only the first part was read by the researcher. In review a Federal Register API query of CMS documents for the unsubsidized individual market returned the 2027 payment notice (proposed and final), and the final rule was read in its first 100,000 characters; it describes market-wide flexibilities and an income-based hardship exemption tied to subsidy ineligibility, but no provision limited to off-exchange coverage. The 2026-09-23 agent and broker rule was not read. Short-term plan non-enforcement is discussed in c14-44, not here. Court proceedings on the Marketplace rule were not checked. Update from the primary-source lift: the first 100,000 of 139,569 characters of the final 2027 payment notice were read (summary, bronze, catastrophic, standardized option and hardship provisions); the last 39,569 characters were not read. In the portion read, no provision applies only to off-exchange or unsubsidized coverage. The Marketplace Integrity final rule was not re-read. In independent review the remaining 39,569 characters of the Federal Register page were read: they cover penalty factors, risk adjustment recalibration and sequestration, and contain no provision limited to off-exchange or unsubsidized coverage (HHS declined separate individual and small group risk adjustment models); the page text ends mid-discussion, so the full rule as published was not read.
